title: Styling and Flexbox
summary: StyleSheet, style arrays and how React Native Flexbox differs from the web: column by default, unitless sizes and no cascade.

sections.title: Styles are objects
sections.body:
Styles are plain JavaScript objects with camelCase keys: `backgroundColor`, `marginHorizontal`, `borderRadius`. Numbers are density-independent pixels (dp, called points on iOS), so `16` means the same physical size on every screen. Percentages are strings: `width: '50%'`.

`StyleSheet.create` validates styles in development and lets you refer to them by name. The `style` prop also accepts an array; later entries override earlier ones, and falsy entries are ignored, which makes conditional styles easy.

sections.title: Flexbox defaults
sections.body:
Every `View` is a flex container. The differences from the web:

- `flexDirection` defaults to `column`, not `row`.
- `alignContent` defaults to `flex-start` and `flexShrink` to `0`.
- `flex: 1` means "grow to fill the space"; a positive `flex` number is shared in proportion between siblings.
- `position` is `relative` by default, and `absolute` positions against the parent.
- `gap`, `rowGap` and `columnGap` are supported in current versions.

A screen that renders nothing is often a `View` with no `flex: 1`, so it has zero height.

sections.title: Layout engine
sections.body: Layout is computed by a C++ Flexbox implementation (Yoga) off the JS thread, then applied to native views. You read the result with `onLayout`, which reports `{ x, y, width, height }` after layout. Use `useWindowDimensions()` for the screen size, which updates on rotation, rather than reading `Dimensions` once.

sections.title: Flattening styles
sections.body:
Native code receives one flat object. `StyleSheet.flatten(style)` walks nested arrays left to right, skips `false`, `null` and `undefined`, and merges objects so the last value wins. Libraries call it when they need to read a computed style, such as a color passed through props.

Exercises here run as TypeScript in a browser sandbox with no React Native runtime, so they model this logic as plain functions and reducers. The same functions drop straight into a real app: call them from a component, a hook or a store.

pitfalls: Expecting rows by default and wondering why items stack vertically.
Using CSS strings like `'16px'`; sizes are unitless numbers.
Creating new style objects inline on every render in hot list rows instead of using `StyleSheet.create`.
Expecting styles to cascade from a parent `View`.

gotchas.question: Two siblings have `flex: 1` and `flex: 2` in a 300 dp tall column. How tall is each?
gotchas.answer: 100 dp and 200 dp. Free space is shared in proportion to the `flex` values (1:2) when neither has a fixed height.

gotchas.question: What does `StyleSheet.flatten([{ padding: 4 }, false, [{ padding: 8, margin: 2 }]])` return?
gotchas.answer: `{ padding: 8, margin: 2 }`. Arrays are flattened recursively, falsy entries are skipped and later values win.

gotchas.question: Why does a screen-level `View` with a background color show nothing?
gotchas.answer: Its height is decided by its content. Without `flex: 1` (or an explicit size) an empty container has zero height.
